learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the main tools of Mathematical Analysis, as well as knowledge of infinitesimal calculus, differentiation, integration, and their applications, regarding both functions of a single variable and functions of several variables.
Acquire the autonomy to use this knowledge as tools for evaluation and interpretation in various fields.
Acquire communication skills characterized by rigor and clarity.

syllabus_topics: Inverse function; elementary functions and their inverse
Bounded sequences; Monotone sequences; Infinite and infinitesimal. Related theorems
Derivatives of inverse function, of the composition of functions, of elementary functions
Main integration's methods: decomposition in sum, by parts, of rational functions
Bernoulli's and other types of equations

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (includes theoretical questions and discussion of second written test exercises)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of two partial written tests and an oral exam. The first partial written test is graded out of thirty and remains valid up to and including the December exam session. The second partial written test is evaluated concurrently with the oral exam. The final grade is based on a weighted average of these evaluations.
